Resolves #18732

`DemoADragMenuNL:86` has been red in every `#17844` census, and it is the evidence `#13158`'s closure gate cites for **three** ADR 0029 §4.1 grains — drag proxy, drop-indicator overlays, commit animation. The engine is correct; two assertions were not.

**The arm's premise was false for this document.** It expected the chips suppressed over the editor zone, on the stated premise that *"the hovered node IS the chips' root target"*. It is not. The chips dock against `dockModel.root` (`PreviewProducer.mjs:377` gates on `root.nodeId !== zone.nodeId`, and `Workspace#resolveDockableRoot` supplies `dockModel.root`), and Demo-A's root is an **edge-zone** holding `editor-tabs` at center and `side-tabs` at right. Neither tabs zone is that boundary, so the full menu lights over both — `Expected: 5, Received: 9`.

Counting cannot separate the two hovers, so flipping `5` to `9` would have made both assertions identical and deleted the arm's only discrimination. The arm now reads the candidate set instead: **the cross re-aims at whatever is hovered while the chips keep docking against the arrangement.** The root id is read from the document rather than written in, because an edge drop replaces `dockModel.root` with the wrapping split.

The suppression the arm meant to witness is not lost — it is covered where it can actually fire, at `DockPreviewProducer.spec.mjs:339`, against a synthetic document whose root IS the hovered zone. I nearly added a second copy of that test before finding it.

**A second defect was hiding behind the first.** With the chips assertion repaired, the arm failed further down at `326 < 326`: the edge-bottom preview bound required *strictly less than half the zone*, and a split preview at the default 0.5 ratio is exactly half — unsatisfiable by construction. It is now bounded on both sides: not the whole zone (which is what proves it re-targeted away from `tab-into`), and not collapsed.

No file under `src/` changes.

Evidence: L3 (the Neural Link journey run on this checkout, green at head, red on dev, and red under an engine mutation) → L3 required, because no CI workflow selects this Brain-gated spec.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The ticket body had the failure direction backwards, and I have corrected the record.** I filed it from the census error's *title* — `the 5-position cross, chips omitted` — and read that as chips missing. The title names the expectation; only the received value names the observation, and it was 9 against 5: chips **lighting** where the spec wanted them suppressed.
- **The ticket's "stale `outerRect`"-style engine hypothesis is not what happened.** I wrote AC-1 to explicitly forbid assuming the engine was wrong, and the capture confirmed it: the producer's gate is correct and self-consistent. The spec was wrong on both counts.
- **A second repair the ticket did not scope.** The edge-bottom bound was masked by the first failure. It is in scope by necessity — the arm cannot pass without it.
  **It is a corrected two-sided retarget bound, not a strictly stronger one** (@neo-gpt-emmy's R-note). On this zone (height 652) the old predicate was `h < 326` and the new one is `163 < h < 648`, so a value like `h = 489` passes now and failed before. What it buys is correctness — the old bound was unsatisfiable against an exactly-half split preview — plus a lower bound the old one never had. Exact fraction and side geometry are already covered by `DockPreview.spec` at this head, so no further geometry assertion is added here.
- **No new unit test.** I wrote one for the suppression rule and then found `DockPreviewProducer.spec.mjs:339` already covers all three cases. Reverted rather than shipped; a duplicate test is accretion.
